title: Version numbers: three parts set by the release job from the pull request's type
seam: .github/workflows/release.yml, .github/workflows/ci.yml, orion.sh version functions, baselines/global/GLOBAL_CLAUDE.md, tests/run.sh, CLAUDE.md
story: orion's version is now three numbers, such as 2.0.0, and nobody raises it by hand: the release job picks the next version from the type at the start of each pull request title and adds the next whole number as a tag so projects on the old script keep being offered updates. Every pull request gets a title check, and the ORION_VERSION file is gone. The session-start update offer, orion status, the status-bar offer and the personal-rules offer read three-part versions, old whole numbers count as older, a project installed just before a release was tagged is not offered it again, and one following another branch records the version of the files it has.

checks.steps: In a throw-away git repo holding a copy of orion (orion.sh, skills/, baselines/), commit, tag the commit v38 and v2.3.4, then run `bash <copy>/orion.sh init --project <empty-dir> --yes --no-statusline` and `bash <copy>/orion.sh status --project <empty-dir>`.
checks.expected: Line 5 of <empty-dir>/.claude/orion/VERSION reads 2.3.4, and status prints `version:    orion 2.3.4,`.

checks.criterion: A project with a whole number on line 5 is offered the update, and its next update writes the three-part number
checks.steps: In a project installed from that copy with --source <copy>, set line 5 of .claude/orion/VERSION to 38. Add a commit to the copy and tag it v2.4.0, then run `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh check --force`, then `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh update`.
checks.expected: check prints one JSON line offering an update from orion 38 to orion 2.4.0; after update, line 5 reads 2.4.0.

checks.criterion: An install made just before its release was tagged gets no repeated offer
checks.steps: Continue from the previous check, then tag the copy's same commit v2.4.1. Run `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh check --force`, then `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh update`.
checks.expected: check prints nothing; update says `already at`, and line 5 now reads 2.4.1.

checks.criterion: A project following a ref other than main records the version of the files it fetched
checks.steps: In the copy, run `git branch old <first commit>` (the commit tagged v2.3.4). In the project, set "ref": "old" in .claude/orion/config.json, then run `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh update --force` and `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh status`.
checks.expected: Line 5 reads 2.3.4, not main's newer 2.4.1, and status prints `version:    orion 2.3.4,`.

checks.criterion: The title check fails on a title with no valid type
checks.steps: Run `bash .github/scripts/release-version.sh title "Add a thing"`, then `bash .github/scripts/release-version.sh title "feat(x): a thing"`.
checks.expected: Exit 1 with a message naming the valid form, then exit 0.

checks.criterion: The release job sizes one version tag per release, adds the next whole-number tag beside it, and tags nothing on a commit an earlier release shipped
checks.steps: In a throw-away repo, tag v39 and v2.0.0, commit a change to skills/a.md with subject `fix: a`, run `bash <orion>/.github/scripts/release-version.sh next` and tag what it printed; add a commit to skills/a.md with subject `feat: b`, run it again and tag what it printed; then `git checkout HEAD~1` and run it once more.
checks.expected: v2.0.1 and v40, then v2.1.0 and v41, then nothing.
